### **Loading Libraries**
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(p8105.datasets)
  data("instacart")
```

### **Loading Data**
```{r}
instacart_df = 
  instacart |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  group_by(
    product_id, product_name, department
  ) |> 
  summarize(
    n_purchases = n(),
    mean_cart_position = mean(add_to_cart_order),
    reorder_rate = mean(reordered)
  ) |> 
  ungroup()
```

### **Scatterplot**: 
*Average cart position vs reorder rate across departments*

* no missing variables through skimr::skim(instacart)
* view(instacart_df) showed that mean_cart_position follows a right skewed histogram distribution; justifies scatterplot decision on the x_axis
* skimr::skim(instacart_df) showed p75=18 for n_purchases and p100= 18726; rounded up to 20 as cutoff point
* After finding `r n_distinct(pull(instacart, department))` departments, print(n=21) listed total number of categories; removed "missing" category in my department filter to better show scatterplot
```{r}
instacart |> 
  count(department) |> 
  arrange(desc(n)) |> 
  print(n=21)
```

```{r}
instacart_df |> 
  filter(department %in% c("dairy eggs", "produce", "canned goods", "beverages", "deli", "snacks", "pantry", "frozen", "meat seafood", "household", "bakery", "personal care", "dry goods pasta", "babies", "other", "breakfast", "international", "alcohol", "bulk", "pets")) |> 
  filter(n_purchases >=19) |> 
  mutate(text_label = str_c("Product: ", product_name, "\nPurchases: ", n_purchases)) |> 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~mean_cart_position,
    y = ~reorder_rate,
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",
    color = ~department,
    colors = "viridis",
    text = ~text_label,
    alpha = 0.5
  )
```
Scatterplot indicates that products placed earlier in the cart tended to be reordered more. Purple-blue categories, such as alcohol, beverages, and canned goods seem to be have an earlier mean cart position. Snacks are notably concentrated around the middle of the cart with an average reorder_rate.

### **Boxplot**: 
*Number of products per order vs day of the week*

* Note labels for days of the week are not given in the dataset; interpretation is contingent upon the assumption that 0 is Monday or some day in the beginning of the week
```{r}
instacart |> 
  group_by(order_id, order_dow) |> 
  summarize(n_products = n()) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(order_dow = as.factor(order_dow)) |> 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~order_dow,
    y = ~n_products,
    color = ~order_dow,
    type = "box",
    colors = "viridis"
  )
```

Produces seem to be ordered the most on Mondays, with Tuesday has the greatest variability and outliers in the number of products purchased per order.

### **Bar Chart**: 
*Number of orders vs hour of the day*

```{r, warning = FALSE}
instacart |> 
  count(order_hour_of_day) |>
  arrange(order_hour_of_day) |> 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~order_hour_of_day,
    y = ~n,
    color = ~n,
    type = "bar",
    colors = "viridis"
  )
```

Greatest number of orders seem to be purchased around the middle of the day from 10 am to about 4 pm, with the least amount of orders made from about 12 am to 6 am.
